member.remarks:
This method will iterate over the data in the ArbitraryData collection. For each line of data, it will attempt to round each value to a specified number of decimal places as provided by the ArbitraryDataRoundingPlaces array. If the rounding is successful, it will then write each rounded value to the file, separating each value with a comma.
Here is an example of how to use the WriteArbitraryFormattedDataToFileV2 method:
Dim sw As New StreamWriter("data.txt") Dim arbitraryDataRoundingPlaces() As Integer = {2, 0, 3} Dim arbitraryData As New List(Of List(Of String)) From { New List(Of String) From {"1.23456", "5.6789", "2.34567"}, New List(Of String) From {"7.89123", "4.5678", "9.01234"} } WriteArbitraryFormattedDataToFileV2(sw, "data.txt", True, "Temperature Data") sw.Close()
Expected output in data.txt: 1.23,6,2.346 7.89,5,9.012

member.name: M:General.clsIndividualSweepCsvHandler.ReadLabViewWavelengthDataFile(System.String)
member.summary: Reads LabView-generated wavelength data from a specified file and extracts specific measurements.
member.param: Path and name of the file containing the wavelength data.
member.remarks: This function is tailored for use with the coarse tuning test, allowing the re-analysis of mirror map data from LabView files. The data file is expected to have a specific structure: - The initial lines may contain metadata like time and temperature. - The data format is specified, typically including mirror1 current (mA), mirror2 current (mA), wavelength (nm), and other measurements. - The actual data follows a line containing "data:". The function reads the file line by line, starting data extraction after encountering "data:". It only extracts the first three values from each line, corresponding to mirror1 current, mirror2 current, and wavelength, respectively. The data is stored in three arrays: X, Y, Z, corresponding to mirror1 values, mirror2 values, and wavelength values.
member.example:
Usage:
ReadLabViewWavelengthDataFile("path_to_file.csv")
